Can a language model supply the information needed for its own inexpensive critic?

text: We test whether a small value head on the actor’s existing hidden states can guide PPO as well as a conventional critic, at lower fitting and memory cost.
textPreview: We test whether a small value head on the actor’s existing hidden states can guide PPO as well as a conventional critic, at lower fitting...

text: The LLM writes a solution one token at a time.
textPreview: The LLM writes a solution one token at a time.

text: A value estimate asks: “How likely is this unfinished solution to succeed?”
textPreview: A value estimate asks: “How likely is this unfinished solution to succeed?”

text: Compare semi-gradient TD and LSTD under matched data, features and compute.
textPreview: Compare semi-gradient TD and LSTD under matched data, features and compute.

text: This is a hypothesis test. A conventional critic can still win; that outcome is informative.
Clipped probability ratios support several updates on one sampled batch.

text: Actor hidden states can support a low-cost value baseline for verifiable rewards.
textPreview: Actor hidden states can support a low-cost value baseline for verifiable rewards.

text: Least-squares Bellman evaluation motivates an LSTD critic solver.

The RL problem in one page
textPreview: The RL problem in one page

text:
state  sₜ = (question, tokens before t)
action  aₜ = next token
terminal reward  rₜ = 1 if Math-Verify says correct, else 0
textPreview: state  sₜ = (question, tokens before t) | action  aₜ = next token | terminal reward  rₜ = 1 if Math-Verify says correct, else 0

text: The reward arrives at the end. Every earlier token needs a credit signal.
textPreview: The reward arrives at the end. Every earlier token needs a credit signal.

text: The critic predicts the chance that the current prefix will eventually earn reward 1 under the current actor.
textPreview: The critic predicts the chance that the current prefix will eventually earn reward 1 under the current actor.

text: Causal rule: read φθ(sₜ) before choosing aₜ.
textPreview: Causal rule: read φθ(sₜ) before choosing aₜ.

text: The value target is a success probability under the binary terminal reward, although an unconstrained linear head may predict outside [0, 1].
PyTorch + FSDP update the actor and PPO critic. Checkpoints, rollouts and reports remain separate for PPO and GRPO.
textPreview: PyTorch + FSDP update the actor and PPO critic. Checkpoints, rollouts and reports remain separate for PPO and GRPO.

text: One combined Slurm job: two GPUs for PPO, two GPUs for GRPO.
textPreview: One combined Slurm job: two GPUs for PPO, two GPUs for GRPO.

text: The architecture is an editable diagram. Slurm handles allocation; the container provides the pinned runtime; VERL owns the algorithmic loop; our code supplies prompts, rewards, configuration, launch orchestration and audits.

δₜ = rₜ + γV(sₜ₊₁) − V(sₜ)
Aₜ = Σₗ (γλ)ˡ δₜ₊ₗ
ρₜ = πθ(aₜ|sₜ) / πold(aₜ|sₜ)
L = min(ρₜAₜ, clip(ρₜ)Aₜ)
textPreview: δₜ = rₜ + γV(sₜ₊₁) − V(sₜ) | Aₜ = Σₗ (γλ)ˡ δₜ₊ₗ | ρₜ = πθ(aₜ|sₜ) / πold(aₜ|sₜ) | L = min(ρₜAₜ, clip(ρₜ)Aₜ)

text: One answer per question in this pilot. A separate critic predicts values and GAE spreads the terminal signal backward.
textPreview: One answer per question in this pilot. A separate critic predicts values and GAE spreads the terminal signal backward.

text: Four answers per question. Answers above their group mean get positive advantage; below-mean answers get negative advantage.
textPreview: Four answers per question. Answers above their group mean get positive advantage; below-mean answers get negative advantage.

text: No critic and no GAE in this baseline.
textPreview: No critic and no GAE in this baseline.

text: Both methods use the same actor, prompt, reward contract and clipped policy update. Their variance-reduction mechanisms differ.
Reuse the actor representation. Learn only a small head.
textPreview: Reuse the actor representation. Learn only a small head.

φθ(sₜ)
= hidden state of the prefix
before action aₜ
textPreview: φθ(sₜ) | = hidden state of the prefix | before action aₜ

text: Semi-gradient TD:  w ← w + α δₜ φθ(sₜ), with the next-state prediction detached.
textPreview: Semi-gradient TD:  w ← w + α δₜ φθ(sₜ), with the next-state prediction detached.

text: LSTD: solve the regularized batch equations  (A + ηI)w = b.
textPreview: LSTD: solve the regularized batch equations  (A + ηI)w = b.

text: The initial comparison has fresh trajectories, no cross-policy replay, causal pre-token features, matched features/data/regularization/initialization and equal-data plus equal-fitting-time controls.
Use Math-Verify; separate wrong answers, parse failures and truncation.
textPreview: Use Math-Verify; separate wrong answers, parse failures and truncation.

text: Validate conventional PPO/GAE, critic updates and checkpoint evidence.
textPreview: Validate conventional PPO/GAE, critic updates and checkpoint evidence.

text: Hold Qwen fixed; compare TD-small, TD-large, LSTD and return regression.
textPreview: Hold Qwen fixed; compare TD-small, TD-large, LSTD and return regression.

text: Connect each lightweight critic to fresh-policy PPO.
textPreview: Connect each lightweight critic to fresh-policy PPO.

text: Use ≥3 seeds; report accuracy per generated token and GPU-hour.
textPreview: Use ≥3 seeds; report accuracy per generated token and GPU-hour.

text: Controls: prompt-level cross-fitting, no initial cross-policy replay, detached critic fitting, matched regularization, and honest compute accounting.
textPreview: Controls: prompt-level cross-fitting, no initial cross-policy replay, detached critic fitting, matched regularization, and honest compute...

text: If return regression predicts well but TD(0) does not, test matched TD(λ) and LSTD(λ) before concluding token-level value learning fails. Critic λ is distinct from GAE λ.
Pilot reports prove that the machinery runs. They do not prove improved math accuracy or a useful critic.
textPreview: Pilot reports prove that the machinery runs. They do not prove improved math accuracy or a useful critic.

1  Evaluate base, PPO and GRPO on 500 held-out questions.
textPreview: 1  Evaluate base, PPO and GRPO on 500 held-out questions.

textPreview: Same prompts, greedy decoding and Math-Verify. Report wrong to right and right to wrong changes.

textPreview: 2  Freeze the actor and benchmark the critics.

text: Compare TD-small, TD-large, LSTD and return regression on held-out prefixes and continuations.
textPreview: Compare TD-small, TD-large, LSTD and return regression on held-out prefixes and continuations.

textPreview: 3  Run short online PPO pilots with the best heads.
